title: extension: side panel's Fill/Attach can skip the first-time confirmation before the first state delivery
body:
## Summary

The side panel's `currentOrigin` is fed only from `state?.origin ?? null` in `follow()`'s `subscribeAnswerState` callback. Before the **first** async state delivery, `currentOrigin` is `null`, `hostOf(null)` is `null`, and `mountFirstFillConfirm`'s `confirm()` early-returns `true` on a null host — so a Fill (or Attach) clicked in that window writes to the page with no first-time confirmation shown.

This is the same defect class as #1227, which was fixed for the popup. It is **not** fixed for the panel, and deliberately so — see below.

## Why the popup's fix doesn't transfer

The popup now resolves the origin on demand via `tabs.query` at click time, which works because opening the popup **is** the toolbar-click gesture that grants `activeTab`.

The panel follows arbitrary tabs via `tabs.onActivated`/`onUpdated`. `activeTab` is gesture-scoped, so for a followed tab the user never clicked there is no grant and no readable url. The panel needs a different design.

## Scope of the exposure

Narrower than the popup's was:

- `job-tools.ts` starts `let trusted = true` and only flips on a delivered `render(state)`, and `follow()` calls `jobTools.render(state)` only inside the subscription callback — so the controls are clickable while connected and before the first delivery.
- **After** the first delivery the window closes: an untrusted/absent state makes `isPageTrusted` false and the gated line replaces the controls, and any *trusted* state is an `AnswerState` whose `origin` is a required string (`answer-state.ts`, `isAnswerState` checks `typeof s.origin === 'string'`). So a reachable panel Fill implies a non-null origin.

So this is a pre-first-delivery race, not a permanent absence.

## Suggested fix direction

Treat a null origin as **untrusted** rather than as "no host to confirm against" — i.e. the panel's controls should not be actionable until an origin is known, mirroring the popup's new fail-safe. Worth checking whether `mountFirstFillConfirm`'s `if (!siteHost) return true;` early return should also become a refusal, but that needs an audit of every caller first: it exists for callers that legitimately have no host.

_Found while reviewing the fix for #1227; reported rather than widened into that PR._

title: desktop: LinkedIn import via DOM capture keeps site-branded title and falls back to hostname as company
body: ## Summary When the extension imports a LinkedIn job posting using its DOM-capture ("Scan mode") path, the desktop backend's generic HTML fallback produces a title still carrying the page's site-branding suffix and a company name that is just the URL hostname, even though the real employer name is present elsewhere in the captured markup. ## Environment Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. ## Steps to reproduce 1. As a logged-in LinkedIn user, open a job view page (`https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/`). 2. Trigger the extension popup or side panel and click Import. ## Expected - Title: the job title alone (e.g. "Javascript Developer"). - Company: the real employer name (e.g. "Digital Waffle"). ## Actual - Title is saved as the whole `` tag verbatim, including site branding, e.g. `"Javascript Developer | Digital Waffle | LinkedIn"`. - Company is saved as the URL host, e.g. `"www.linkedin.com"`. - DOM capture itself succeeded (the stored job description was ~8,000 characters of real content, including the text "Company logo for, Digital Waffle" from an `<img alt>`) — the extraction heuristic just never looks at that signal. - Frequency: reproduced on the one LinkedIn posting tested; deterministic given the code path (not timing-dependent). ## Evidence Imported application record: `title` = `"Javascript Developer | Digital Waffle | LinkedIn"`, `company` = `"www.linkedin.com"`, with the correct job URL and a full-length job description containing the real company name as incidental text (not extracted as a field). ## Root cause Scan-mode Import (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/import_flow.rs:252`) parses the extension's captured DOM directly via `scraping::scrape_url::parse_from_html`, bypassing the dedicated LinkedIn board handler (which needs the desktop's own authenticated session and isn't needed when the DOM was already captured from the owner's logged-in browser). That generic path has two gaps: - `parse_generic_html` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:918-931`, called at `mod.rs:468`) takes the first `<title>`/`<h1>` element's full text with no trimming of a trailing " | SiteName" suffix. - `parse_generic_company` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:939-969`) only checks JSON-LD `hiringOrganization.name` and `meta[property="og:site_name"]`; neither is populated by LinkedIn's authenticated, client-rendered job page. Its caller (`mod.rs:549`) then falls back to the bare URL host (`parse_generic_company(html).unwrap_or(host)`). ## Suggested fix direction In the generic fallback: strip a trailing `" | <site>"`/`" - <site>"` suffix from the title when it matches a known site name or `og:site_name`; and add a company fallback that looks for a distinctive `<img alt="Company logo for, X">`-style pattern (or similar DOM signal already present in LinkedIn's captured markup) before giving up and using the host.

title: extension: Import silently captures the embedding page for iframe-embedded ATS boards
body:
## Summary

When a job board is embedded on a company's own careers page via a cross-origin `<iframe>` (a common pattern for Ashby, and potentially other ATS platforms with embeddable widgets), clicking **Import** on the wrapper page silently imports the WRAPPER page's own title/heading instead of the job posting inside the iframe. There is no error, no partial-capture warning — only a very low match-fit percentage in the success toast, which is easy to miss or not recognize as a signal that anything went wrong.

## Environment

- Extension 0.154.0 (store build)
- Desktop app 0.154.0
- Windows 11, Chrome

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a careers page that embeds an ATS job board (e.g. Ashby) in a cross-origin `<iframe>`, with the specific job selected via a query parameter in the outer page's URL.
2. Click the extension's toolbar icon to open the popup on that tab.
3. Click **Import this job**.

## Expected

Either the real job posting inside the iframe is captured and imported, or the user is clearly told the capture may not reflect the actual posting (e.g. the existing "couldn't read the description — open AI Job Hunter to paste it" partial-import warning), so they know to check/complete the record manually.

## Actual

The import succeeds with a confident-looking message ("Imported \"<wrapper page's own heading>\". Open AI Job Hunter → Applications to view it.") built from the OUTER page's own `<title>`/`<h1>`, not the job. The only anomaly visible to the user is a very low percent-fit suffix on that same message — there is no explicit warning, and the resulting Application record has the wrong title/company and no real job description. Frequency: deterministic, every time, for any cross-origin-iframe-embedded ATS whose wrapper page happens to render a non-empty title/heading (not timing-dependent).

## Evidence

Reproduced against a live Ashby-embedded careers page; the popup's success message named the wrapper page's own "Careers at <company>"-style heading rather than the actual job title, at a single-digit percent fit. (Sanitized — no personal data; the specific company/job-posting URL used for the repro is omitted here as it is not needed to understand or fix the defect.)

## Root cause

- `apps/extension/src/background.ts:474-477` (`captureTabHtml`) injects the DOM-capture script via `browser.scripting.executeScript({ target: { tabId }, files: ['content.js'] })` with no `allFrames` option, so `content.ts`'s capture (`document.documentElement.outerHTML`) can only ever see the top-level document — a cross-origin iframe's content is unreachable without `host_permissions` this extension does not request. (The README already documents this exact no-allFrames/activeTab-only trade-off for the Fill feature — `apps/extension/README.md`'s "Known limit — assisted autofill fills the TOP-LEVEL document only" note — but not for Import.)
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:466-548` (`parse_from_html`) falls through to the whole-document `<title>`/first-`<h1>` fallback when the extension's job-root hint finds nothing in the outer page (which it never can here), picking up the wrapper page's own heading.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:129-191` (`canonical_job_url`) and `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/scraping/ats_ref.rs:131-138` (`ashby_slug`) only recognize a URL whose OWN host is the ATS's host — nothing detects/resolves an embedded ATS iframe on an unrelated host.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/import_flow.rs:103-105` (`usable()`) treats ANY non-empty title as usable, so the wrapper page's own heading (never empty) suppresses the existing "couldn't read the description" partial-import warning (`apps/extension/src/job-tools/job-tools.ts:80-127`) that would otherwise flag this case.

## Suggested fix direction

Either direction addresses the silent-wrong-data problem without requiring new cross-origin permissions:

1. **Cheap, in line with the existing Fill precedent**: extend the README's documented Fill limitation to Import, and have the extension/desktop side detect "no job-root hint was found in the outer document AND the page contains a same-page ATS iframe" (a `document.querySelector('iframe[src*="ashbyhq.com"], iframe[src*="greenhouse.io"], ...')` check in `content.ts` is enough signal) to surface the iframe's own URL to the user (e.g. "This job is embedded — open it directly at <iframe src> to import").
2. **Fuller fix**: teach `usable()`/`import_flow.rs` that a title sourced only from the whole-document fallback (never from JSON-LD, `__NEXT_DATA__`, or the extension's own job-root hint) is a weaker signal, and route that case through the existing `partial` warning path instead of treating it as a clean success.

title: Prep tab's Cancel does not actually stop the in-flight AI request (still billed in full)
body:
## Summary

Clicking **Cancel** on a Prep-tab on-demand draft (`Draft company brief` / `Draft salary answer`) correctly reverts the extension UI back to the draft button, but the underlying AI-provider request is **not aborted** — it runs to completion server-side and consumes real tokens/cost, exactly as if Cancel had never been clicked.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome, provider `ollama-cloud` / `gpt-oss:20b`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the side panel's **Prep** tab on any job with no existing company-brief/salary-answer content.
2. Click **Draft salary answer**.
3. Immediately click **Cancel** (verified via script: the Cancel button is clicked at the first opportunity, effectively 0ms after the draft starts, well before the ~3.5s the request actually takes).
4. Compare the extension's own click timestamp against the desktop app log (`AI Job Hunter.log`, UTC).

## Expected

Cancelling stops the outbound AI request; no further tokens are spent for that draft once Cancel is clicked.

## Actual

The app log shows the request completing in full, at the same duration/token cost as an un-cancelled draft:

```
[21:32:34] [ai] → req=29 provider=ollama-cloud model=gpt-oss:20b endpoint=/chat/completions streaming=true
[21:32:37] [ai] stream start job=job-6a6f0064-...
[21:32:37] [ai] stream end provider=ollama-cloud model=gpt-oss:20b answerLen=112 thinkingLen=43 finishReason=Some(End) usageIn=2413 usageOut=43 empty=false
[21:32:37] [ai] ← req=29 ... status=200 duration=3467ms ok=true
```

The extension UI reverted cleanly to `Draft salary answer` (no stray result, no error) — the bug is invisible from the UI; it only shows up as wasted spend in the app log.

## Suspected cause

`apps/extension/src/lib/bridge.ts`'s `cancelCurrent()` → `supersedeAnyPendingAssist()` does send an `assist.cancel` frame (`cancelAssist()`, `apps/extension/src/lib/bridge.ts:2014-2022`) and correctly stops relaying further chunks/settles the promise client-side — but nothing downstream on the desktop side appears to abort the actual provider HTTP stream for this code path. `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/answer_assist_topic.rs` (the Prep tab's on-demand `topic` extension to `answer.assist`, PR4) has no references to `cancel`/`register`/`AbortHandle`/`spawn` at all, despite its own doc comment claiming it "grounds it through the EXACT SAME draft pipeline every other `answer.assist` call uses — same gate, same `ai_research` bucket/limiter, **same registry**, same streaming frames." The real cancellable-job registry lives in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/assist_registry.rs` (`cancel`/`cancel_all`, backed by a `JobCanceller`/`AbortHandle`) — worth confirming whether a topic-mode draft's job actually gets `register`ed into it, or whether it silently bypasses registration.

## Impact

"AI spend is real money" — a user who reflexively cancels a draft (wrong topic clicked, changed their mind, etc.) is still billed for the full generation every time, with zero indication anything went wrong.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Answers-tab free-text instruction is ignored by chips and dropped server-side on Regenerate
body:
## Summary

The Answers tab's free-text "Instruction for '<question>'" box has no effect on the drafted/rewritten text, in either of the two ways a user could plausibly use it: clicking a TONE/LENGTH chip while it's filled in ignores it completely (chips carry their own hardcoded preset/instruction), and using "Regenerate"/"Draft this answer" — the one control that actually transmits the typed instruction to the desktop app — also has no effect, because the desktop's draft-mode compose path never reads the `instruction` field at all.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome, Ollama Cloud (`gpt-oss:20b`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Answers tab on a drafted row with an existing version (e.g. "Tell us more").
2. Type a specific instruction into "Instruction for '…'", e.g. "Focus only on the websocket migration story, keep it under 120 characters total."
3a. Click a TONE or LENGTH chip (e.g. "Shorter"), OR
3b. Click "Regenerate" (the button that is documented — via the UI hint "Regenerate rethinks it from your résumé" — to be the one that uses free text).

## Expected

At least path (b) — Regenerate — incorporates the typed instruction (topic focus and/or the 120-character limit) into the new version, since it is the control that sends `instruction` in its request payload.

## Actual

Neither path reflects the instruction at all:
- (a) Chip click: result is close in length to the pre-chip text and still about React/Next.js/Tauri/etc — nothing about the requested "websocket migration" topic.
- (b) Regenerate click: result (v6, ~650 characters) still restates unrelated highlights from the résumé — no mention of "websocket" anywhere, and nowhere close to the requested 120-character limit. The desktop AI request log confirms a real, successful call was made (`req=21`, `status=200`, `duration=5663ms`) — this is not a silent failure, the instruction is simply never reaching the model.

## Root cause

- **Chips never read the free-text box.** `apps/extension/src/answer-tools/answer-tools.ts:165-190` — every `TONE_CHIPS`/`LENGTH_CHIPS` entry carries its OWN fixed `preset` or `instruction` string (e.g. `Warmer` → `"Make this warmer and more personal…"`). The click handler (`answer-tools.ts:392-401`) sends only `chip.preset`/`chip.instruction` — the view-local `instructions` map (what the user typed) is never referenced there at all.
- **Regenerate DOES send it, but the backend drops it.** `answer-tools.ts:488-503`, the Regenerate/"Draft this answer" handler, sends `mode: 'draft'` plus `instruction: instructions.get(row.id)` when non-empty (line 500) — this part is correct. But server-side, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/answer_assist.rs`:
  - `parse_instruction`/`resolve_rewrite_instruction` (lines 388-417) are documented as "rewrite mode only" and are only invoked via `validate_rewrite_fields`, which is itself only called `match mode { AssistMode::Rewrite => Some(validate_rewrite_fields(payload)?), AssistMode::Draft => None }` (lines 720-723).
  - `build_user_message`, the draft-mode prompt builder (lines 551-592), takes `question, resume, job_description, company_brief, web_notes, salary_range` — there is no parameter for a free-text instruction anywhere in its signature or body.
  - So a `mode:'draft'` request's `instruction` field is parsed nowhere in the whole compose path; it is present on the wire and then simply never read.

## Suggested fix direction

Either wire the free-text instruction into the draft-mode prompt (extend `build_user_message` with an optional "additional instruction from the candidate" parameter, fenced the same way `question` is, and have `resolve_answer_assist`'s `AssistMode::Draft` arm read `payload.get("instruction")` and pass it through), or — if draft mode is intentionally never meant to take a free-text instruction — remove/hide the instruction box for the draft/Regenerate action (or gray it out with a note) so it isn't presented as something that shapes the next draft when it silently does nothing. The current combination (a visible, always-enabled input, a UI hint implying Regenerate is exactly the control that uses it, and total silence about the fact that nothing happens) is the misleading part.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Accept into field works once per row, then fails and orphans the draft on the next Rescan
body:
## Summary

In the extension's Answers tab, "Accept into field" only works ONCE per row. After the first successful accept fills a previously-empty field, every subsequent Accept on that same row (e.g. after clicking Regenerate to produce a new version) fails immediately with "Could not find this field — the page may have changed." — even though the field is untouched, still visible, and holds exactly the text the first Accept wrote. If the user then clicks Rescan to recover, the real-world field is split into TWO panel rows: a fresh one with no draft history, and an orphaned one that keeps the AI-drafted versions but permanently loses its "Accept into field" button, stranding that work.

## Environment

extension 0.154.0 store build, desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome, Ollama Cloud (`gpt-oss:20b`) as the AI provider.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an application form with an empty text/textarea question (confirmed on Ashby, e.g. jobs.ashbyhq.com/linear/.../application, "What country are you based in?").
2. Open the side panel → Answers tab → expand that row → "Draft this answer" → "Accept into field". Confirm the page field now shows the drafted text.
3. Click "Regenerate" on the same row (produces a new version, v2/v3/…).
4. Click "Accept into field" again, without Rescanning in between.

## Expected

The new version replaces the old text in the (now non-empty) field, the same way "Accept" worked the first time.

## Actual

Step 4 fails instantly: `"Could not find this field — the page may have changed."` The field itself is confirmed present and unchanged (verified by reading the live DOM value directly: still holds exactly what the first Accept wrote). Reproduced 1/1 cleanly; the message is actively misleading since nothing about the page changed.

If the user then clicks **Rescan** to try to recover: the Answers tab count inflates (4 questions → 5 in my repro) and the SAME real field now shows as two separate rows — one labelled "…Filled" with no version history (Accept works fine on this one), and the original row (still showing its full v1..vN draft history) with NO "Accept into field" button at all — only Copy/Regenerate remain, so the user's edited draft can never be written to the page again without manually copy-pasting it themselves.

## Root cause

- `writeRowText` (`apps/extension/src/background.ts:1954-1988`) branches on `row.field.kind` ('empty' vs 'filled') to pick `injectAnswerFill` (empty-field path) vs `injectAnswerReplace` (filled-field path). On a successful write, its state update (lines 1979-1986) only refreshes `field.currentText` — it never flips `field.kind` from `'empty'` to `'filled'`.
- So a second Accept on the same row still takes the `injectAnswerFill` branch, which calls `locateQuestionField` (`apps/extension/src/lib/answers-capture.ts:247-256`) — this only searches `emptyCandidateFields`. Since the field is no longer empty, it is absent from that candidate set, the occurrence count no longer matches, and the function returns `null` → the fixed `NOT_FOUND` result (`apps/extension/src/lib/answer-fill.ts:44-47`), surfaced verbatim as "Could not find this field — the page may have changed."
- The Rescan-time row-split is a direct consequence: `fieldRowId(kind, question, index)` (`apps/extension/src/lib/answer-state.ts:197-199`) bakes `kind` into the row's own id. A fresh scan of the now-genuinely-filled field produces a `filled:…` id, which is different from the original `empty:…` id the row was created under, so `buildRows`'s carry-over-by-id logic (`answer-state.ts:254-332`) cannot reunite them — it creates a brand-new "Filled" row for the live field and leaves the old row to survive only because it "holds versions" (per that function's own doc comment), now with `field` undefined and therefore no Accept action (`canAccept`, gating `apps/extension/src/answer-tools/answer-tools.ts:459`).

## Suggested fix direction

When `writeRowText` succeeds against an `'empty'`-kind field, also flip `field.kind` to `'filled'` in the same state update (alongside `currentText`) so a second Accept correctly takes the `injectAnswerReplace` path without needing a Rescan. Separately, `buildRows`'s carry-over might consider matching a prior row by `(question, index)` ignoring `kind` when the exact-id match misses (or the field ref could migrate to `filled:...`'s row rather than orphaning the original), so a Rescan doesn't strand drafted versions were the kind-transition to happen anyway.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: extension: Attach always reports "more than one résumé field" on Greenhouse-style forms with a separate cover-letter upload
body:
## Summary
`isResumeFileInput`'s fallback rule matches a file input as "résumé-like" when its `accept` attribute lists document types (`pdf|\.docx?|msword|wordprocessingml`), with no requirement that the name/id/label also mention résumé/CV. On a very common real-world ATS pattern — a separate, optional "Cover Letter" file upload sitting next to the "Resume/CV" upload, both accepting the same document types — this fallback matches BOTH inputs, so Attach always reports "Found more than one résumé upload field on this page — attach it yourself," even though the correct field is trivially identifiable by its id/name alone.

## Environment
Extension 0.154.0 (store build), desktop app 0.154.0, Windows 11, Chrome. Reproduced on a real Greenhouse application form (`job-boards.greenhouse.io`).

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a Greenhouse job application page that has both a résumé upload and a separate cover-letter upload.
2. Open the side panel's Documents tab, pick a résumé source, and click "Attach résumé to this page".

## Expected
Attach locates the résumé-specific field and attaches to it (its `id="resume"` is unambiguous).

## Actual
`"Found more than one résumé upload field on this page — attach it yourself."` — reproduced 3/3 tries (deterministic, not flaky). DOM inspection of the two file inputs:
```json
[{"id":"resume","accept":".pdf,.doc,.docx,.txt,.rtf"},
 {"id":"cover_letter","accept":".pdf,.doc,.docx,.txt,.rtf"}]
```
Both inputs share the exact same `accept` list, so both match `RESUME_FILE_ACCEPT_RE`, and neither `id` needed to say "resume" for the false match — the `cover_letter` field matched purely on `accept`.

## Root cause
`apps/extension/src/lib/submit-watch.ts:110-131`:
```ts
const RESUME_FILE_TEXT_RE = /resume|curriculum|lebenslauf|(?:^|[^a-z])cv/;
const RESUME_FILE_ACCEPT_RE = /pdf|\.docx?|msword|wordprocessingml/;
...
return RESUME_FILE_TEXT_RE.test(textSignal(el)) || RESUME_FILE_ACCEPT_RE.test(accept);
```
The two signals are OR'd with no way for one to disambiguate the other, and the `accept`-only match is too generic — "accepts a PDF or Word doc" is true of nearly every document upload field on a job application form, résumé or not.

## Suggested fix direction
When the accept-based match alone would produce more than one candidate on the page, prefer any candidate whose name/id/label/aria-label matches `RESUME_FILE_TEXT_RE`, and/or explicitly exclude a field whose text signal matches a cover-letter pattern (`cover.?letter|anschreiben|motivation`) even if its `accept` list matches.

_Found during an end-to-end test of the published 0.154.0 extension's Documents tab against the 0.154.0 desktop app._

title: settings: give the browser extension its own settings nav item and section
body:
## Summary

The browser-extension settings have grown into a full area of their own (pairing and token, connection status, four consent switches: assisted autofill, AI answer drafting, auto-track, save-answers-on-submit, plus their notices). They still live as one section inside **Settings → Accounts**, where they are hard to find and crowd the accounts page. Give the extension its own entry in the Settings sidebar and its own section.

## Proposal

- Add a top-level **Browser extension** item to the Settings sidebar (`NAV_GROUPS` / `SectionId`), rendering the existing `ExtensionBridgeSection` (moved out of `apps/desktop/src/renderer/features/settings/components/accounts/`, where it is mounted by `AccountsSettingsTab`).
- Keep the `ajh://settings/extension` deep link (the extension popup's "Find my token" button, `FocusTarget::ExtensionPairing` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/deeplink/mod.rs`) landing on the new section, with the existing focus/scroll highlight (`ui-store` flag consumed by `ExtensionBridgeSection`).
- Update the settings search index (`features/settings/lib/search-index.ts`) and the help/support content that points at the old location.
- Update every piece of copy that tells the user to go to "Settings → Accounts → Browser extension". Today that wording appears in:
  - desktop refusal strings sent to the extension: `extension_bridge/{mod,status_update,document_export,agent_read,agent_call,answer_assist,answers_save}.rs`, `tray/mod.rs`, `deeplink/mod.rs`
  - the extension: `apps/extension/src/connection-status/connection-status.ts`, `apps/extension/README.md`
  - shared protocol constants: `packages/shared/src/ipc/extension-protocol-constants.ts`
  - translations (`packages/translations/src/locales/*`), `packages/prompts/src/workspace/index.ts`
  - the landing privacy page (`apps/landing/src/components/privacy/sections/{Extension,Footer}.tsx`) and the root `README.md`

## Notes

- The published extension build embeds the old wording in its own copy. Until the next Chrome/AMO release, installed extensions will still say "Accounts". The deep link is the robust path either way.
- No behaviour change to any consent switch, gate or wire verb. This is a navigation and copy move only.

## Acceptance criteria

- Settings shows a separate **Browser extension** nav item; the Accounts page no longer contains the extension section.
- `ajh://settings/extension` opens that section and highlights the pairing area.
- No remaining "Accounts → Browser extension" wording in the repo (except changelog/history).
- Existing `ExtensionBridgeSection` tests pass; sidebar/search tests cover the new item.
